column11: two published shares multiplied against HORIZON 1 Cohort A1's own criteria. (1) 0.06317 unresectable stage III NSCLC given chemotherapy and radiation as first treatment: of 239,602 lung cancers in SEER over 2000 to 2013, 33,507 were unresectable stage III NSCLC and 12,865 received chemotherapy and radiation (Hansen RN et al., BMC Cancer 2020;20:276, PMC7132866), which is 5.369% of all lung cancer diagnoses and 5.369 / 0.85 = 6.317% over the NSCLC pool; the share azn_oleclumab.csv carries for this identical setting. (2) 0.026 ALK-rearranged: 'Overall, the prevalence of ALK rearrangement was 2.6% in aNSCLC patients (519 of 19,895 patients)' (Allen TC, Xiao Y, Yang B et al., 'Anaplastic lymphoma kinase rearrangement prevalence in patients with advanced non-small cell lung cancer in the United States: retrospective real world data', Oncotarget 2021;12(23):2308-2315, doi 10.18632/oncotarget.28114, PMC8590819, open access, read 2026-11-14; Flatiron Health across about 280 US cancer clinics, stage IIIB to IV diagnosed January 2015 to May 2019). 0.06317 x 0.026 = 0.001642, about 316 patients a year
column12: the concurrent-only filter azn_oleclumab.csv applies (84.2%) is deliberately NOT applied, because HORIZON 1 admits sequential chemoradiation as well as concurrent. The ALK share is measured in advanced disease rather than stage III, which is the weaker half of this row; ALK-rearranged patients are younger and more often never-smokers, and no free US source gives the share by stage. A tiny pool, and honestly so: HORIZON 1 has enrolled 68 patients in total across its cohorts

column10: share of each year's eligible patients
column11: ANCHOR, measured: 262 of 426 US patients with unresectable stage III NSCLC who started concurrent chemoradiation, 61.5%, went on to consolidation durvalumab (Arunachalam A et al., PLoS One 2024;19(11):e0314156, PMC11588217, US Oncology Network, starts 2017 to 2019); death (28.3%) and progression (22.2%) were the main reasons the rest did not. It is the book's one measured US capture for an anti-PD-(L)1 added to a definitive chemoradiation regimen given with curative intent, and azn_oleclumab.csv already carries it. MULTIPLE 1.0, and the biomarker is the reason it is taken whole where azn_oleclumab.csv halves it. Oleclumab would share the consolidation slot with durvalumab; alectinib would replace it, because HORIZON 1 Cohort A1 randomises the two head to head in the ALK-positive slice and a win would make alectinib the consolidation for those patients rather than an addition to it. The ceiling is then the share of the eligible pool that reaches consolidation at all, which is what 61.5% measures
column12: case for lower: ALK-positive stage III patients are increasingly moved to a tyrosine kinase inhibitor before or instead of chemoradiation, which would take them out of this pool before the consolidation decision. Case for higher: alectinib is already the asset's standard of care in the adjacent resected and metastatic settings, so the prescriber is the same one
